s1.syndrome_frame: Pruritic papular eruption with annular lesions and cornoid lamellae on histopathology
salient_findings: Rapidly spreading intensively pruritic papules on extremities
Erythematous, annular papules with cornoid lamellae on histopathology
Asymptomatic brown flat papules on the face
key_facts: Female patient in her 50s
3-month history of symptoms
No remarkable medical or family history
No concurrent medications
Previous treatment with topical steroid ointments and oral compound glycyrrhizin tablets had no effect
Lesions are scattered, erythematous, annular papules up to 5 mm wide
Palms, soles, and oral mucosa are not involved
Laboratory tests showed no abnormal findings
Histopathology revealed mild hyperkeratosis, parakeratosis, atrophy of the epidermis, and individual cell dyskeratosis
Slight infiltrate of lymphocytes, histiocytes, and eosinophils in the upper dermis

shortlist.label: Disseminated superficial porokeratosis
shortlist.why_kept: Matches clinical presentation of pruritic papules with cornoid lamellae on histopathology

shortlist.label: Porokeratosis
shortlist.why_kept: Shares similar histopathological features, including cornoid lamellae and parakeratosis

shortlist.label: Linear porokeratosis
shortlist.why_kept: Variant of porokeratosis that could present with similar lesions, although less likely given the scattered distribution

shortlist.label: Darier's disease
shortlist.why_kept: Could present with similar skin lesions, although the histopathology and clinical context are not as strongly supportive

shortlist.label: Grover's disease
shortlist.why_kept: Less likely but still plausible given the presence of pruritic papules and some histopathological overlap

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of scattered, erythematous, annular papules with histopathological findings of cornoid lamellae, parakeratosis, and mild hyperkeratosis is consistent with disseminated superficial porokeratosis. The absence of involvement of palms, soles, and oral mucosa and the lack of response to previous treatments also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Linear porokeratosis
rejected.why: Linear distribution of lesions is not mentioned in the case

rejected.label: Porokeratosis
rejected.why: Too broad, as porokeratosis encompasses several subtypes

rejected.label: Darier's disease
rejected.why: Typically presents with greasy, crusted papules in seborrheic areas and nail changes, which are not described in the case

rejected.label: Grover's disease
rejected.why: Characterized by sudden onset of pruritic papules, often with a distinctive histological feature of suprabasal acantholysis, which is not mentioned in the case
